## Real-CI-log verification on change 2367 patchset 1 — run 33230196661 (`Verified`: SUCCESS). Acceptance criterion 2 does NOT pass, and the reason is a second manifest consumer the plan missed.

Evidence read from `gh api repos/navapbc/rebar/actions/jobs/<id>/logs --allow-escape-sequences` (note: `gh run view --job=N --log` returns an EMPTY log while the parent run is still in progress — that empty log scored 0/0/0 on all three greps, i.e. a clean vacuous pass, which is exactly the false negative the liveness anchor exists to catch. It caught it.)

Five jobs, identical result:

| job | anchor `Successfully installed uv version 0.12.7` | `Could not determine uv version` | `Fetching manifest data` | `Found version for uv in` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 99041728105 lint + type-check | 1 | 0 | 1 | 1 |
| 99041728081 pip-audit | 1 | 0 | 1 | 1 |
| 99041728162 pytest ubuntu py3.11 | 1 | 0 | 1 | 1 |
| 99041728119 pytest macos py3.13 | 1 | 0 | 1 | 1 |
| 99041728143 eval discipline | 1 | 0 | 1 | 1 |

The ordered assertion, on `lint + type-check`:

    [ANCHOR — PRESENT]  02:59:37.3853812Z Successfully installed uv version 0.12.7
    [SOURCE  — PRESENT] 02:59:36.7625196Z Found version for uv in /home/runner/work/rebar/rebar/pyproject.toml: 0.12.7
    [FALLBACK — ABSENT] count=0   (was present on every job before the change)
    [MANIFEST — STILL PRESENT] 02:59:36.7637479Z Fetching manifest data from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/astral-sh/versions/main/v1/uv.ndjson ...

**What passes.** The anchor proves the step ran and that the INSTALLED version equals the pin (a separate claim from the message disappearing). `Found version for uv in .../pyproject.toml: 0.12.7` proves the new single source is the thing being read. The `Could not determine uv version` fallback is gone on every job.

**What does NOT pass, and why.** `setup-uv` makes TWO independent uses of the manifest, and the plan only accounted for one:

1. **Version resolution** — `resolveUvVersion` -> `LatestVersionResolver`/`RangeVersionResolver` -> `getLatestVersion`/`getAllVersions`. Reached ONLY when no version is determinable locally. **The pin removes this one.**
2. **Artifact lookup** — `setup-uv.ts` calls `tryGetFromToolCache` and, on a miss, `downloadVersion`, whose FIRST statement is `const artifact = await getArtifact(version, arch, platform, manifestUrl)` (`src/download/download-version.ts:42`). This is UNCONDITIONAL: the manifest supplies the download URL, so it is fetched even when the version was resolved locally with no network at all. A GitHub-hosted runner's tool cache never contains uv on a fresh job, so the miss is guaranteed.

Because `getArtifact` shares `cachedManifestData` with the resolver, there was only ever ONE fetch per job — before the change the resolver triggered it, after the change the artifact lookup does. The count is unchanged at 1, so **the `##[error]fetch failed` failure mode this bug reports is NOT eliminated**.

I checked whether this is a version problem: it is not. `v10.0.1`, the newest release (2026-08-14), calls `getArtifact` unconditionally at the same place. Nor can a committed local manifest sidestep it — `fetchManifestResponse` uses Node's `fetch()`, which does not accept `file:` URLs, and the `manifest-file` input is documented as a URL.

**Consequence for this ticket.** Acceptance criteria 1, 3, 4, 5 (anchor) and the guard criteria are met; criterion 2 as written ('no manifest fetch from raw.githubusercontent.com') is NOT. The pin fully fixes the SUPPLY-CHAIN half of the bug — the resolved uv can no longer change between runs or between publishes with no repository change — but not the availability half. Change 2367 is being re-worded so it claims only what it does, and the residual fetch is tracked as a discovered follow-up rather than quietly folded in: removing it needs a different mechanism (pre-seeding the runner tool cache, or not installing uv through this action), which is a materially different plan than the one reviewed here.

**Not closing this ticket.** Escalating to the operator for the call on whether 2367 lands as the partial fix with the follow-up, or whether this bug stays open until the fetch is actually gone.
